{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-05",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["Internal admin portal", "SAML Service Provider handler", "Role mapping / authorization check", "Session management"],
    "dataStores": ["Portal session store"],
    "externalServices": ["Corporate identity provider (SAML IdP)"],
    "trustBoundaries": ["Internet to internet-reachable admin portal", "Portal to corporate identity provider", "Browser-mediated SAML assertion flow"],
    "dataClasses": ["credentials"],
    "exposure": "public",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Forged role attribute in SAML assertion grants admin access",
      "scenario": "Any employee (or an attacker who obtains a low-privilege assertion) edits the role attribute in the SAML response posted by their own browser. If the portal reads the attribute without verifying the XML signature over the whole assertion, the attacker sets role=admin and gains full administrative control of the internal portal.",
      "component": "SAML Service Provider handler / role mapping",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "the portal reads the role attribute from the assertion to decide admin access" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V9.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-347", "CWE-290"],
      "plainLanguage": "A normal user could change 'role: user' to 'role: admin' in the login message and become an administrator.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Verify assertion signature before reading role attributes",
        "given": "a SAML response is posted to the admin portal",
        "when": "the portal extracts the role attribute to decide admin access",
        "then": "it only does so after validating the XML signature over the assertion against the configured IdP signing certificate, and rejects unsigned, self-signed or signature-only-on-response assertions"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "Assertion accepted from the wrong issuer or for the wrong audience",
      "scenario": "An attacker obtains a valid SAML assertion from a different tenant or a test IdP they control and posts it to the portal's assertion consumer endpoint, which is reachable from the internet. If Issuer, Destination and AudienceRestriction are not pinned to the corporate IdP and this portal, the attacker authenticates as any subject they choose, including an admin.",
      "component": "SAML assertion consumer endpoint",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Employees sign in to the internal admin portal through SAML single sign-on with the corporate identity provider." },
        { "quote": "The portal is reachable from the internet." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V9.2.2"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-290"],
      "plainLanguage": "A login ticket issued by someone else's identity system could be accepted by our portal.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Pin issuer, audience and destination",
        "given": "an assertion arrives at the assertion consumer service",
        "when": "the portal validates it",
        "then": "it rejects the assertion unless Issuer equals the configured corporate IdP entity id, AudienceRestriction equals this portal's entity id, and Destination equals this endpoint URL"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "Captured SAML response replayed to log in as another employee",
      "scenario": "An attacker who captures a SAML response from a browser (shared workstation, proxy, browser history or logs of the POST body) replays it to the internet-facing portal. Without an assertion-ID replay cache, NotBefore/NotOnOrAfter enforcement and InResponseTo matching to a pending request, the attacker gets an authenticated admin session without any credentials.",
      "component": "SAML Service Provider handler",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Employees sign in to the internal admin portal through SAML single sign-on with the corporate identity provider." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V9.2.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-294"],
      "plainLanguage": "Someone could reuse a copied login message to sign in as that person.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Reject replayed assertions",
        "given": "a valid signed assertion that has already been consumed or is outside its validity window",
        "when": "it is posted again to the portal",
        "then": "the portal rejects it based on a stored assertion id replay cache, NotBefore/NotOnOrAfter checks and an InResponseTo value matching a request this portal issued"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "XML signature wrapping bypasses assertion validation",
      "scenario": "An attacker takes their own legitimately signed assertion and wraps it so the signed element and the element the portal actually reads differ (signature validated on one node, role and NameID read from an injected sibling). Many hand-rolled SAML parsers are vulnerable; the attacker ends up with an assertion that passes signature checks but carries attacker-chosen identity and role.",
      "component": "SAML XML parsing and signature validation",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "the portal reads the role attribute from the assertion to decide admin access" }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-347"],
      "plainLanguage": "A trick in the XML can make the portal check the signature on one part but trust a different, attacker-written part.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Read only the signature-verified assertion node",
        "given": "a SAML response containing multiple Assertion or Attribute elements",
        "when": "the portal resolves the subject and role",
        "then": "it uses a maintained SAML library, resolves values only from the exact node covered by the verified signature, and rejects responses containing more than one assertion"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Admin authorization decided solely by an IdP attribute with no server-side role record",
      "scenario": "Admin access depends entirely on an attribute asserted at login time. Anyone who can influence the directory attribute (helpdesk, HR self-service, group self-join, IdP admin) silently becomes a portal admin with no approval in the portal, and revocation at the IdP does not take effect until the existing session expires.",
      "component": "Role mapping / authorization check",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "After login, the portal reads the role attribute from the assertion to decide admin access." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V8.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-269"],
      "plainLanguage": "Whoever can edit a user's directory attribute can hand out admin rights to our portal, and taking them away is slow.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Authorize admin actions against portal-side roles",
        "given": "an authenticated employee whose assertion claims the admin role",
        "when": "they request an administrative function",
        "then": "the portal checks a portal-owned authorization record for that user on every request, and an allowed value set for the mapped attribute, rather than trusting the login-time attribute alone"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Unvalidated RelayState used as a post-login redirect",
      "scenario": "An attacker sends an employee a login link whose RelayState points at an attacker-controlled site. After a genuine SSO login the portal redirects there, letting the attacker phish for re-authentication or capture tokens appended to the URL. Because the portal is internet-reachable, the link works from anywhere.",
      "component": "SAML login initiation / RelayState handling",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The portal is reachable from the internet." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-601"],
      "plainLanguage": "A crafted login link could bounce the user to a fake site right after they sign in.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Restrict post-login redirects to this portal",
        "given": "a login request carrying a RelayState or return-url parameter",
        "when": "the portal redirects the user after a successful assertion",
        "then": "it only redirects to a relative path on the portal's own host and otherwise sends the user to the default landing page"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "XML external entity injection through the posted SAML response",
      "scenario": "An unauthenticated attacker posts a SAML response containing an external entity or DTD to the internet-facing assertion consumer endpoint. If the XML parser resolves entities, the attacker reads local files such as the signing key or configuration, or forces server-side requests into the internal network from a host that straddles the internet boundary.",
      "component": "SAML XML parser",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The portal is reachable from the internet." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-611"],
      "plainLanguage": "A malicious login message could make the server read its own files or call internal systems.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Parse SAML with entity resolution disabled",
        "given": "a SAML response containing a DTD or external entity reference",
        "when": "the portal parses it",
        "then": "the parser rejects the document with DTD and external entity processing disabled, before any signature or attribute handling"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Internet-exposed admin portal with no second factor or network restriction",
      "scenario": "The administrative portal is directly reachable from the internet, so any stolen or phished corporate credential immediately yields admin access from anywhere, and any IdP-bypass path (local fallback login, legacy session cookie, exposed non-SSO endpoint) is attackable by the whole internet rather than only on-network staff.",
      "component": "Internal admin portal exposure",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The portal is reachable from the internet." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V6.4.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-306"],
      "plainLanguage": "Because the admin site is open to the internet, one stolen staff password is enough for an attacker anywhere to get in.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Gate internet access to the admin portal",
        "given": "a request to the admin portal from outside the corporate network",
        "when": "the user attempts to reach any administrative page",
        "then": "access requires a successful SSO login with phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication enforced by the IdP (or the portal is restricted to the corporate network/VPN), and no non-SSO login path is exposed"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "Admin actions cannot be tied to a specific employee",
      "scenario": "The portal identifies users from assertion attributes only. If it keys sessions on a mutable attribute such as email or display name instead of a stable NameID, an attacker who gets an attribute changed at the IdP can inherit another employee's admin identity and history, and later disputes about who performed an administrative change cannot be resolved.",
      "component": "Session management / identity mapping",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "After login, the portal reads the role attribute from the assertion to decide admin access." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-345"],
      "plainLanguage": "If accounts are matched on something changeable like an email address, one person can end up inside another person's admin account.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Key accounts on a stable identifier",
        "given": "an assertion for an employee whose email or display name has changed",
        "when": "the portal links the login to a portal account",
        "then": "it matches on the immutable IdP subject identifier and records that identifier with every administrative action, never matching on email or display name alone"
      }
    }
  ]
}
